title: Runtime fallback & triage console orchestration - NimbusRx walkthrough
next_steps: Samir to share Dedicated pricing + pilot terms by 2027-04-28
Ava to send security & SOC2 docs; include KMS/HSM integration notes
Schedule 1-week live pilot run for request-forensics on 2027-05-04 with Evan and Jared
action_items: Samir Patel: Send pricing + pilot terms by 2027-04-28
Ava Chen: Share security pack + KMS integration doc by 2027-04-27
Maya Ortiz: Provide sample request traces and SLOs by 2027-04-29
summary: Intro demo of Redwood Console features for runtime fallback orchestration, request-level forensics, and debugging flows. Focus on how console ties tracing, request logs, and KV cache fallbacks to help ops triage LLM inference errors and latency-cost tradeoffs.
topics: Playback / request replay for root cause
transcript: 00:00:00 - Samir Patel: Hey everyone — thanks for carving out time. Quick intros? We got about 50 minutes, want to show the Console's runtime fallback and debugging flow end to end.
00:00:07 - Maya Ortiz: Hi — Maya here, platform. Evan's on SRE and Jared's going to hand over traces. Priya is on for context. Thanks Samir.
00:00:12 - Evan Rhee: Hey, real quick, our main goal is to reduce P50 latency and cut wasted tokens during retries. Also SOC2 stuff will matter — we'll ask about encryption.
00:00:22 - Ava Chen: Perfect. We'll start with a live demo: tracing, request inspector, then fallback rules. I'll flag places where cost/latency levers live.
00:00:35 - Luca Moreno: Also show model-variant routing and a canary roll to simulate degradation.
00:00:40 - Priya Desai: Good. We have a hard stop at 5:05 so please keep to the flow.

00:01:05 - Ava Chen: Alright loading the Console — first screen is the Request Inspector. You can paste a request ID or search by user session. I'm entering a sample request from Nimbus that exhibits a long tail token churn.

00:01:24 - Ava Chen: Notice at the top we show a timeline: request start, model selection, KV cache hit/miss, token generation windows. The KV cache shows a 28% miss rate for this workload — that's where a prefix cache would help.
00:01:41 - Jared Kim: That 28% seems high — our client scenarios often repeat prompts. Is this prefix-only or whole-request cache?
00:01:49 - Ava Chen: Good question — this is prefix/KV cache by conversation context. You can configure TTLs and keys. We also surface which token ranges missed so you can tune similarity windows.
00:02:10 - Evan Rhee: Can we see the raw logs tied to the request? We want to correlate the model call to our service span.

00:02:18 - Ava Chen: Yep — pull up the trace correlator. It joins Redwood request id to customer span via trace id header. Here's the span map — you can jump into the full logs, including the raw prompt and model variant selected.
00:02:40 - Maya Ortiz: Sometimes our infra sees a fallback to a lower-cost model and that increases hallucinations. How do we control that behavior?
00:02:49 - Samir Patel: We'll demo fallback policies — you can set by latency SLO, region availability, or cost thresholds. You can also pin routes to disallow fallback for sensitive routes.

00:03:05 - Ava Chen: Starting a simulation: I trigger an artificial slowdown on the primary model. Watch the policy evaluate — it falls back to a quantized variant in the same family and annotates the trace with 'fallback: model-quant-v2'.
00:03:25 - Priya Desai: That annotation is helpful — does the trace include token-level confidence or generation deltas?
00:03:33 - Ava Chen: We include model variant metadata and a quality score if you upload eval prompts. For live scoring we'd pipe your eval harness results to the Console and surface regressions.
00:03:50 - Evan Rhee: On auditing — we need immutable logs for audits. Are request payloads retained, and is there KMS encryption at rest?

00:03:58 - Samir Patel: Hosted keeps encrypted logs with customer-specific KMS keys on Dedicated/Private. We can redact PII at ingest, and retention is configurable per tenant. We'll send the SOC2 package.
00:04:20 - Maya Ortiz: Good. For pilot we'd like to run Dedicated for a week and push realistic traffic to see fallbacks under load.
00:04:27 - Samir Patel: That aligns with our recommended pilot. We'll include burst capacity and guardrails for canarying.

00:04:40 - Ava Chen: Back to the trace — here's a request playback widget. You can replay the exact model inputs against a pinned model or a variant, and we capture tokenization and end-to-end latency broken down by kernel and sequence length.
00:04:58 - Jared Kim: Playback — does it charge tokens? We need a sandbox mode.
00:05:06 - Ava Chen: Playback runs in a sandbox and is metered separately; you can run it against a no-cost local quantized runtime for comparison. We show estimated token cost per run though.

00:05:32 - Ava Chen: Now here's a common ops pattern: a spike in latency due to KV cache misses followed by a cascade of retries. The Console surfaces retry storms and groups related requests so you can throttle or change batching.
00:05:56 - Evan Rhee: Do you show batching windows and batch sizes used? Our inference pipeline relies on micro-batching.
00:06:04 - Ava Chen: Yes — continuous batching metrics are visible per model pool; you can set max batch sizes and timeouts. We also annotate where batching caused head-of-line blocking.
00:06:25 - Maya Ortiz: On the model routing UI — can we set different policies per route? E.g., low-latency route for search, cost-optimized for batch scoring.
00:06:33 - Luca Moreno: Exactly. You define routes with selector rules and attach a policy set. Policies can be hierarchical — org default, team override, route pin.
00:06:47 - Priya Desai: For compliance we need role-based access to redaction toggles and to prevent developers reading raw prompts. RBAC?
00:06:55 - Samir Patel: Console supports RBAC & SSO. You can restrict view of raw prompts, set redaction policies, and require approval for playback runs that include PII.
00:07:10 - Evan Rhee: Quick tangent — how do you instrument our app to pass the trace id? Do you have SDKs?
00:07:16 - Ava Chen: We provide lightweight SDKs (Python, Node, Go) and a header mapping guide. If you have existing tracing (Jaeger/OTel) we auto-correlate via traceparent header.
00:07:32 - Jared Kim: We use OTel with custom sampling. Will Redwood's sampling interfere?
00:07:38 - Ava Chen: No, we respect your sampling. We only ingest what you send and can augment spans with model metadata client-side or server-side.
00:07:52 - Maya Ortiz: Can we see a failed case? We had a recent incident where a routing misconfiguration doubled token usage.

00:08:00 - Ava Chen: Pulling an incident trace — here, you can see the routing rule incorrectly matched and selected a full-context model for simple completions. The Console highlights the rule eval log and proposed fix.
00:08:22 - Ava Chen: Note the timeline shows a sudden jump in generated tokens at t+2s. There's a 'rule-misfire' tag and the UI surfaces the exact route expression that matched.
00:08:39 - Priya Desai: How do we prevent misfires? Test harness? Linting rules?
00:08:46 - Luca Moreno: We include a policy simulator that runs route rules against sample traffic. You can run a 'dry-run' mode to detect unexpected matches before deploying.
00:09:05 - Evan Rhee: For rollouts, can we do canary by percentage and then auto-roll back on regression in generation quality?

00:09:12 - Ava Chen: Yes — canary rollouts can use both latency and quality signals. If your eval suite reports quality drop above threshold, the orchestrator will auto-failover and notify via webhook.
00:09:30 - Maya Ortiz: That webhook integration — do you support our internal pager system and Slack?
00:09:35 - Samir Patel: Slack, PagerDuty, webhooks are supported. Teams often wire an alert to SRE and product and attach the failing request IDs.
00:09:52 - Jared Kim: On the KV cache tuning — can we export a report that maps common prefixes to hit/miss and recommended TTLs?
00:09:58 - Ava Chen: Yes, the Optimize tab generates suggestions: TTL, quantization profile, batch sizing. It gives an estimated cost delta and expected latency change.
00:10:18 - Priya Desai: For Dedicated vs Hosted — what are the SLA differences and footprint? We're leaning Dedicated for PII workloads.

00:10:26 - Samir Patel: Dedicated gives isolated GPU pools, private networking, and single-tenant logs. SLAs for p99 latency and availability are higher; we can share the contract. Private (on-prem) options exist too.
00:10:41 - Evan Rhee: Sizing question: how do you recommend instance types for our workload? We have many short chatty calls and some long-form generation.

00:10:49 - Luca Moreno: The Optimize toolkit recommends a mixed pool. Use smaller instances for short calls to reduce cold tokens and a larger pool for long contexts to amortize kernel overhead. We'll include a sizing worksheet.

00:11:12 - Ava Chen: Now demo of a live debug: I search for the request id Maya uploaded. Here we have the request, trace, logs, and a playback run. I'm clicking 'Compare variants' to see generation diffs between model-v1 and quant-v2.
00:11:34 - Ava Chen: The diff view highlights hallucination tokens and confidence heuristics. You can link to the failing eval prompts and open a Jira from the Console.
00:11:52 - Maya Ortiz: Nice. Our legal team requires audit trails for any prompt content that left our VPC. How do you support private deploys?
00:11:59 - Samir Patel: Private deploys can be air-gapped and run a local control plane. Logs can be forwarded to your SIEM or kept on-prem. We'll share the architecture note.
00:12:18 - Evan Rhee: A risk: if we do on-prem, do we lose Console features like the Optimize suggestions?

00:12:25 - Luca Moreno: Optimize runs either in a hybrid model or a packaged agent. We can surface recommendations locally; some cloud-only telemetry options would be disabled per your compliance needs.

00:12:44 - Ava Chen: Switching to the error analysis view: errors are grouped by signature. You can filter by error class, model, or route. For example this batch shows 'tokenization-failure' due to unexpected unicode.
00:13:02 - Jared Kim: We do see occasional tokenization mismatches when customers paste rich text. Any sanity filters we can apply?
00:13:09 - Ava Chen: You can run a pre-tokenization hook in the SDK to normalize input. Console will mark 'pre-tokenization normalized' so you have auditability.
00:13:24 - Maya Ortiz: Is there a way to alert on sudden increases in token per request? We want to catch prompt regressions early.
00:13:31 - Ava Chen: Absolutely — set anomaly alerts on tokens/request or cost per request. Thresholds can be static or anomaly-detected using historical baselines.
00:13:52 - Evan Rhee: Can we run a short chaos test to ensure fallback works under partial region outage?
00:13:58 - Samir Patel: We often run a chaos week as part of onboarding. You can simulate region failure and validate that fallbacks route to the next region or model variant.

00:14:12 - Ava Chen: Quick note: trace text recognition sometimes garbles model names; we've seen transcriptions call 'quantize' 'quant-v 2' as 'quantiv two' — small quirk in the search layer but irrelevant to runtime.
00:14:29 - Priya Desai: (laughs) noted. Any other questions on the Console itself?
00:14:35 - Maya Ortiz: Two asks: one, a short runbook template for incidents that mention Console steps; two, a demo for our SREs that goes deeper on batching and kernel selection.
00:14:45 - Samir Patel: We'll provide both — runbook template and a technical deep-dive workshop. I'll coordinate scheduling.
00:14:57 - Ava Chen: Last demo piece — I'm enabling a canary that routes 10% traffic to quant-v2 and wire an eval webhook. Triggering a failing eval will auto rollback in 3 mins if regression > 2%.
00:15:18 - Evan Rhee: Good control. How are rollout metrics calculated? Are they sampled or full-stream?
00:15:25 - Ava Chen: By default we sample a high-fidelity stream for the canary and aggregate totals for the rest. You can opt into full fidelity at extra retention cost.
00:15:42 - Jared Kim: Can we export the trace + logs as a single JSON bundle for offline forensic analysis?
00:15:49 - Ava Chen: Yes — 'Export forensic bundle' downloads spans, logs, and playback input. It can be encrypted with customer KMS key.
00:16:05 - Maya Ortiz: Great. A quick procurement Q — what does pilot include and what's the path to Dedicated?

00:16:12 - Samir Patel: Pilot typically includes a 1-week Dedicated sandbox, X hours of engineering time for integration and a runbook. If it meets your SLOs we convert to a reserved capacity contract.
00:16:28 - Priya Desai: Fine — legal will want the security pack. Evan will coordinate the pilot traffic windows.
00:16:36 - Evan Rhee: Sounds good. We'll provision traces and sample traffic. We'll also send a list of banned prompt patterns for redaction tests.
00:16:46 - Samir Patel: Noted. I'll send the pricing and pilot docs. Ava will send security pack. Luca will own the deeper SRE session.

00:16:55 - Maya Ortiz: One more thing — we'd like a short experiment to test whether switching to a different quant profile reduces cost without hurting recall. Can you recommend a quick A/B test design?
00:17:06 - Luca Moreno: Yes — define a control group on your production traffic and a 5% experiment with quant-v2. Use immediate offline evals and a 48-hour rolling window to surface regressions.
00:17:24 - Priya Desai: Perfect. Let's capture that as an action item.

00:17:30 - Samir Patel: Quick recap then next steps: 1) Samir send pilot pricing and contract; 2) Ava send SOC2 + KMS docs; 3) Schedule 1-week Dedicated pilot starting 2027-05-04; 4) Run SRE deep-dive on batching/kernels week of 2027-05-10.
00:17:55 - Maya Ortiz: That works. Thanks team — that demo was very targeted and helped clarify where Console would plug in.
00:18:05 - Evan Rhee: Thanks — we'll follow up with traces and a security contact email.
00:18:12 - Priya Desai: Appreciate the time. We'll loop legal after we get the pack.
00:18:18 - Samir Patel: Thanks everyone. We'll send artifacts and I'll book the next calls. Bye!
00:18:25 - (call ends)
